evidence: Purdue BuildingShapesZip4 FID 826 identifies Beta Theta Pi, 150 Littleton St; Beta Mu and BoilerLink directory sources corroborate the address.
The fresh-open wall base has 19 unique vertices matching all 19 transformed GIS ring vertices with maximum nearest-vertex error 0.0000294 m.
criteria.finding: Identity and building footprint are exceptionally well supported.

evidence: Fresh-open world bounds are X 805.983–827.110 m, Y -417.268–-375.652 m; these align with the exact campus-transformed feature footprint.
GIS aerial overlay supports the location. Facade photo orientation is not independently georegistered.
criteria.finding: Placement and plan dimensions are reliable; facade bearing is not survey-verified.

evidence: The r4 roof shell is one continuous closed mesh: 38 vertices, 73 edges, 37 faces, zero boundary edges, zero nonmanifold edges, and zero zero-area faces.
All 17 top roof facets have upward normals; the 19 side faces and one underside face have expected vertical/downward orientation. Every mesh in the file has nonzero face area.
Previews retain dark-looking seams at some gable/roof intersections; the actual roof shell is continuous, but its shallow ridge and exact heights are photographic estimates.
criteria.finding: The former disconnected roof facets are fixed and topology/normals are sound. Gable intersections still read visually dark/awkward, and no measured roof elevations are available.

criteria.criterion: Facade, entrance, and distinctive photo-backed details
evidence: The six r4 previews show the three-level brick facade, divided sash windows, projecting pale bay with stacked arched openings, central front gable, two dormers, arched entry, and chapter crest; these motifs appear in chapter-house photos.
Facade placement and window spacing are simplified/repetitive. The doorway reads as a pale blank block in the close view, and the arch/crest proportions do not fully capture the photographed entry.
criteria.finding: The primary architectural identity is recognizable and substantially source-informed, with simplified rhythms and a visibly unresolved door detail.

criteria.criterion: Portable materials, modular handoff, and evidence quality
evidence: Fresh-open scene and collection names match contract; 349 mesh objects load in the expected collection.
Six node-based materials reopen; brick, slate, stone, and painted trim use procedural nodes. No external file images are referenced.
Identity, GIS geometry, official chapter-house photo gallery, university listing, Esri aerial, and limitations are documented.
Materials look mottled rather than coursed brick/slate in renders; there is no interior model because no reliable public floor plan was found.
criteria.finding: The file is self-contained and source-documented. Surface texture is stylized, and omission of an unsupported interior is appropriate.

actionable_findings: Adjust the doorway/entry material and proportions so a dark wood door and transom read clearly in the close view.
Reduce dark-looking roof/gable intersection artifacts and review with more even lighting; the closed roof shell itself is watertight and correctly oriented.
Consider a coursed brick and more restrained slate pattern so the native procedural materials read less like mottled noise.
Keep roof heights and the north-south ridge documented as photo-derived estimates; no survey values were found.
No interior revision is required without a reliable public floor plan.
